summary:

summary:
Waymo announced today that it will use Toyota bZ4X electric vehicles that are assembled in Japan for a robotaxi service in Tokyo.
The news builds on the strategic partnership between Waymo and Toyota which was first announced in April 2025.
A team-up between the world’s largest automaker and the world’s leader in autonomous driving obviously has huge implications.
By adding the bZ4X, Waymo is attempting to prove that its autonomous driving technology is compatible with a wide range of vehicle types.
Waymo also says it is continuing to explore integrating its technology into Toyota vehicles for personally owned autonomous vehicles.

title: T-Mobile tells SpaceX there's no room for an MVNO deal
summary:
Click for next articleT-Mobile isn’t interested in turning SpaceX into a wireless partner, and CEO Srini Gopalan isn’t exactly being subtle about it.
Gopalan said T-Mobile evaluates potential MVNO partnerships based on whether they open up new addressable markets, distribution channels, or capabilities.
He doesn't believe a SpaceX deal will accomplish any of those things.
The company would still consider a straight commercial or resale arrangement, but that’s a very different proposition to providing SpaceX access through an MVNO deal.
Verizon CEO Dan Schulman also dismissed an MVNO deal, and AT&T boss John Stankey downplayed the competitive threat.

title: AI-controlled .50-cal gun turrets are becoming a reality of war
summary:

Notably, Brave1 said these turrets took down Russian Geran-5s and Banderols — jet-powered drones and cruise missiles that can reach speeds of 375 to 400 mph.
The turrets do have limited range, making them more useful as a final defense against drones or against low-flying targets.
They'll likely be one of several tools Ukraine is developing to counter Russian jet-powered threats.

title: Alphabet Is in Talks to Join Trump’s Golden Dome Defense Program
summary:
(Bloomberg) -- Alphabet Inc.'s Google is in talks with the US Defense Department to work on a new data security effort underpinning the $185 billion Golden Dome missile defense program, according to people familiar with the matter.
The talks have focused on Google's data storage, networking and cybersecurity capabilities, one of the people said.
Golden Dome is President Donald Trump's marquee defense program to build a layer of defense systems from ground to space that will protect the US from foreign attack.
The effort would mark Google's first publicly known involvement in the Golden Dome program and another sign of how the search engine giant is continuing to lean into national security and defense work.
Both the Pentagon's separate Golden Dome initiatives to pioneer space-based missile interceptors and its command-and-control consortium rely on numerous companies from startups to established primes, unlike past defense programs that have been more typically anchored by a single, large contractor.

title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
summary:

Currently, sites have to signal their AI training preferences separately to each AI company.
The announcement comes as publishers grapple with the continuing influx of AI crawlers scraping their sites and feeding their content into AI models.
OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will restrict their AI crawlers from accessing a site if they encounter the shared token.
Google previously implemented similar controls that allow sites to control whether their content appears in AI search features or is used for AI training, without impacting visibility in search.

title: Google’s latest Nest Learning Thermostat is $60 off just in time for sweater weather
summary:
As the weather cools, it may be worth investing in a smart thermostat to help lower your energy bills.
Right now, Google’s fourth-gen Nest Learning Thermostat is on sale in all three colors for $219.99 ($60 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and The Home Depot, matching its best price of the year and just $10 shy of its all-time low.
Google’s latest Nest Learning Thermostat is its most capable to date, and comes with new features designed to lower energy consumption without sacrificing comfort.
It can also suggest schedule changes to save energy and automatically adjusts the temperature when you’re away.
The Nest Learning Thermostat also improves on its predecessor with a beautifully designed adaptive display that shows your temperature settings, the weather, and the time from across the room.

title: Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk
summary:
“A lot of people want local inference.
And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open-source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center.
But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time.
You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you’re trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment.
And somehow everyone’s— many people’s intuition is the opposite of that.”
